clue.text: Advance payments — one way to get by

parts.note: subs are payments made in advance, as of wages
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A claim that taking money in advance is one method of scraping by.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsist is to survive on meagre means, which is what getting by means.

clue.text: Check support group first

indicators.note: first says the word for group comes before the word for support

parts.note: a set is a group of things
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: An instruction to verify that a support group is put first.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a check or reverse to progress, so the two are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Joining the Globe, aim to be a writer

parts.note: a globe is a ball, a sphere
to point something is to aim it

explanation.surface: An actor hoping to become a playwright by joining the company at the Globe theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Globe' suggests the London theatre, which suits the writing ambition, but here it is just a round object.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint pen is something that writes, so it is a writer in a playful object sense.

clue.text: Question children

definitions.meaning: a matter in question, a point under debate

explanation.definitionFit: Issue means both a disputed point and a person's offspring.

clue.text: They're for educating Rita — lots trained outside university

indicators.note: outside says the shuffled letters go around the university letter
trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: In the play Educating Rita, the heroine is taught at length around her Open University studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' makes TTORIALS, and 'outside' puts that around U. Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about an Open University student and her tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorials are small teaching sessions, so they exist for the purpose of educating students.

clue.text: Beer bottle for Brecht's mother

definitions.meaning: A long-established English brewery and beer brand
bottle is British slang for nerve or bravery
Bertolt Brecht wrote the play Mother ... and Her Children

explanation.surface: Someone fetching a bottle of beer for the mother in a Brecht play.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a beer brand, British slang 'bottle' for nerve, and the surname of Brecht's heroine Mother Courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a British beer brand, means nerve or bravery, and is the title character's name in Brecht.

clue.text: Charming woman left out of group

indicators.note: out of says one letter is removed from the word for group

parts.note: a circle is a group of people, as in a circle of friends

explanation.surface: A charming woman leaving a social group.
explanation.walkthrough: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned Odysseus's men into pigs; 'Charming' means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: The Homeric sorceress charmed men with spells, so she is literally a charming woman.

clue.text: Type of joint found in film studios

definitions.meaning: a ... joint is a coupling allowing rotation in any direction
... Studios is a Hollywood film company

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a mechanical coupling and a major Hollywood studio.

clue.text: Old tennis player's cricket trophy

definitions.meaning: Arthur Ashe was a champion tennis player of the 1960s and 70s
the trophy for England v Australia Test series

explanation.surface: A trophy that once belonged to a tennis star, now awarded at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first definition as ASHE'S, the possessive of Arthur Ashe's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive of Ashe's name and the name of the England v Australia cricket trophy coincide.

clue.text: Not stopping goal? Not so many!

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
less means a smaller amount, not so many

explanation.surface: Someone asking about a goal in a match and being told there are fewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless continues without stopping, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Call heard for works of Hoffmann

indicators.note: heard says the word for call is taken by its sound

parts.note: tails is a call when a coin is tossed

explanation.surface: A request heard for a performance of some pieces by Hoffmann.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tales of Hoffmann is Offenbach's opera based on stories by E. T. A. Hoffmann.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoffmann wrote fantastic stories, collected in the opera title The Tales of Hoffmann.

clue.text: Threads in fashion lost their lustre?

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Asking whether fashionable clothing threads have become dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threads' and 'fashion' suggest clothing, but 'fashion' is a verb: rearrange THREADS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnished metal has become dull, so things tarnished have lost their lustre.

clue.text: Jonathan's producer, perhaps

parts.note: Jonathan looks like a man's name, but it is a variety of eating apple, so its producer is what it grows on

explanation.definitionFit: A Jonathan is an apple variety, and the plant that bears such fruit is this.

clue.text: Man, for example, going west with eastern girl

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means read right to left

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man heading westwards with a girl from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's name, so the answer is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Head and tail of kipper: wretched seafood

indicators.note: head and tail are the first and last letters of the fish's name

parts.note: to feel ill is to feel wretched

explanation.surface: A cook trims a kipper and finds it miserable fare.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, a British breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny crustaceans eaten by whales and sometimes by people, so they count as seafood.

clue.text: A VIP sells assorted toiletries

indicators.note: assorted suggests a mixed selection, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A celebrity selling a range of bathroom products.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip salves are balms for chapped lips, a kind of toiletry.

clue.text: Nutty set with acorns — old people in a tree?

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A set of acorns has fallen, and someone wonders about the old folk up an oak tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty' fits acorns but is the anagram signal; the 'tree' is a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears appear in the upper branches of a family tree, so they are old people in a tree.

clue.text: Fried food served cold with salad

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
roquette, or rocket, is a salad leaf

explanation.surface: A menu item: something fried served cold alongside salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a breadcrumbed roll of filling that is fried, so it is a fried food.

clue.text: Bring down spare seat cover

parts.note: food left over is spare
a throw is a cloth draped over a sofa or chair

explanation.surface: A request to take down a spare cover from a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow a ruler is to bring them down, so the verbs match.

clue.text: One piece of advice concerning starter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a tip is a piece of advice
as to means concerning or about

explanation.surface: Someone offers a single tip about how to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian first course, so it is a starter.

clue.text: Old general with a stronghold, so to speak, on the borders of Phrygia

parts.note: read stronghold as strong hold: a firm hold is a grip

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: An ancient general with a fortress on the edge of Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stronghold' looks like a fort, but 'so to speak' asks for strong hold, A GRIP. Agrippa was Augustus's leading Roman general.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa commanded Augustus's forces at Actium, so he is an ancient general.

clue.text: Novice not a partner of this composer?

definitions.text: Novice not a partner of this composer?

parts.words: Novice not a partner of this composer?
parts.note: a novice is a learner, which sounds like the lyricist Alan Jay Lerner; but a learner is not Lerner, this composer's partner on My Fair Lady

explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Loewe wrote the music for My Fair Lady with lyricist Alan Jay Lerner, whose name sounds like learner.

clue.text: Hartley novel: "Chance"

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel by L. P. Hartley called Chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hartley wrote The Go-Between, so 'novel' poses as a noun. The quote marks on Chance point to the idiom 'not an earthly', British slang for no chance at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase 'not an earthly', the word stands for a chance, as in no hope whatever.

clue.text: Bob Marley, for example, could be a star

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may form something else

explanation.surface: Bob Marley could become a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Marley was a famous follower of Rastafarianism, so he is an example of a Rasta.

clue.text: Divided Balkan city

explanation.definitionFit: The word means divided and is also the name of a Croatian city on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Flag down fisherman

parts.note: to feel blue is to feel down
Saint Peter was a fisherman before becoming an apostle

explanation.surface: An instruction to lower the flag to a fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag down' looks like hailing someone; 'down' is BLUE. The Blue Peter is the flag a ship flies before sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Peter is a blue and white signal flag hoisted when a ship is about to leave port.

clue.text: Beast with dry eyes, initially

parts.note: brut is the term for very dry champagne

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An animal with dry eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a savage animal, so it is a beast.

clue.text: Irrational response when cop pockets a nickel

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece goes in another

parts.note: PC is a police constable, a cop
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: Someone reacts wildly when a policeman takes a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nickel' suggests the US five-cent coin, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden uncontrolled fear, an irrational response to danger.

clue.text: Event in European cellar

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
a vault is an underground room or cellar

explanation.surface: A happening in a European basement.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole vault is an athletics event, so it is an example of an event.

clue.text: Way to go in tavern or theatre

indicators.note: in says the letters are concealed inside the clue words

explanation.surface: Directions to a pub or a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: North is a compass direction, a way to head.

clue.text: Blakey is extremely talkative performer

parts.note: Art Blakey was an American jazz drummer

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters of the word

explanation.surface: The drummer Art Blakey is a chatty performer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, so it is a performer.

clue.text: Bet on every course?

parts.note: each means every one
a way is a course or route

explanation.surface: A gambler backing every racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: An each-way bet backs a horse to win and to be placed; 'course' suggests a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: An each-way bet is a wager on a horse to win or be placed, so it is a type of bet.
